clue.text: Scarlet underwear half-cut harlot wears for work with gangsters

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a vest is an undergarment in British usage

indicators.note: only half the word survives the cut, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A tipsy prostitute shows off her red undies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for tipsy, but here it halves the harlot. Red Harvest is Dashiell Hammett's novel of gang warfare in a corrupt mining town.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammett's novel Red Harvest is a crime story about rival gangs in a corrupt mining town.

clue.text: Where Daisy Miller passes on rambling walk, so we're told

indicators.note: a phrase signalling that a word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to roam is to go on an aimless, rambling walk

explanation.surface: A clue about where Henry James's heroine wanders before her death.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Miller, in Henry James's novella, catches fever after a night visit to the Colosseum and dies in the Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian capital is the city where James's heroine contracts malaria and dies.

clue.text: Book featuring a lot of spice and nude gambolling about

definitions.text: Book featuring a lot of spice

indicators.note: frisking around, so the letters of the word are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A racy book full of spice and naked frolicking.
explanation.walkthrough: The spice reads as sexy content, but Frank Herbert's science-fiction novel centres on the spice melange mined on the desert planet Arrakis.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert's science-fiction novel is built around a precious spice harvested on a desert planet.

clue.text: A source covering Hacked Off for a Murdoch publication

parts.note: the head of a river is its source
a limb hacked off has been severed

explanation.surface: An insider at a Murdoch newspaper leaks to the phone-hacking campaign group Hacked Off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Rupert Murdoch's newspapers and the Hacked Off phone-hacking campaign; the publication is a novel by Iris Murdoch.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch wrote the 1961 novel of that title, a comedy of marital betrayals.

clue.text: Nagini was one in part very current theatre revolutionized!

parts.note: rep, short for repertory, is a kind of theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre production that cast Voldemort's snake in a radical new staging.
explanation.walkthrough: Nagini, Voldemort's snake in Harry Potter, is shown in the Fantastic Beasts films to be a cursed woman, so a snake only in part.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous snake, which Voldemort's pet Nagini partly was, being a woman cursed into serpent form.

clue.text: A work by Charlotte Brontë initially found by wee drips abroad

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a fresh order
only the opening letter of the novelist's surname is used

explanation.surface: A novel by Charlotte Brontë is discovered dripping a little on the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlotte Brontë' reads as one name, but the definition is just 'A work by Charlotte': Charlotte the spider of E. B. White's Charlotte's Web spins one.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, the spider heroine of White's children's book, spins the silken trap whose messages save the pig Wilbur.

clue.text: Tree Talos cut down for Bendini, Lambert & Locke?

parts.note: the setter's pseudonym stands for the setter, so me

explanation.surface: A setter fells a tree for a law practice.
explanation.walkthrough: Bendini, Lambert & Locke is the sinister Memphis law practice in John Grisham's novel The Firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grisham partnership is a business, specifically a company of lawyers.

clue.text: Romantic dialects I mangled when going round Italy

badly damaged, so the letters are reshaped into another order

explanation.surface: A tourist murders the local dialects while wandering round Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mangled' rearranges DIALECTS into DEALSTIC, and 'going round' puts that around I for Italy; the clue's own I leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic person holds unrealistic, high-minded visions, the mark of an idealist.

clue.text: Secretary blunt with writer on Indy every so often

a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: only alternate letters of the newspaper name are taken

explanation.surface: A bluntly spoken secretary who writes for the Independent now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunt' is old British slang for money. The Indy is the Independent newspaper. Miss Moneypenny is M's secretary in the James Bond books.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ian Fleming's Bond novels, Miss Moneypenny is the personal assistant to M.

clue.text: "The nicest thing about feeling happy is that you think you'll never be unhappy again" (Kiss of the Spider Woman, -)

parts.note: a quotation with its source, the dash standing for the author's name

explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine novelist wrote Kiss of the Spider Woman, from which the quoted line comes.

clue.text: Moriarty is one arch-villain primarily found in lair

clue.text: Where you find me in John McGahern's most famous novel?

definitions.text: Where you find me in John McGahern's most famous novel?

explanation.surface: A question asking where to find the speaker in McGahern's best-known book.
explanation.walkthrough: McGahern's 1990 novel of an Irish farming family is titled after the position of the letters ME in the word WOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names McGahern's 1990 novel and also describes the letters M, E placed inside a word for females.

clue.text: Circus performer looking happy with stuff written about performance ultimately

explanation.surface: A grinning circus act with a programme written about the show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circus is John le Carré's name for the British secret service headquarters, where his spymaster works.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Carré's spymaster serves in the Circus, the novelist's nickname for MI6.

clue.text: "Those boobs of yours are - - like God!" (Milan Kundera)

definitions.text: "Those boobs of yours are - - like God!" (Milan Kundera)

parts.words: "Those boobs of yours are - - like God!" (Milan Kundera)
parts.note: a quotation from Kundera with a missing word to be filled in

explanation.surface: A quotation from Kundera awaiting its missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means present everywhere, the attribute of omnipresence ascribed to God.

clue.text: Young sages travelling for places sleuth David Small might know?

explanation.walkthrough: David Small is the rabbi detective in Harry Kemelman's novels, beginning with Friday the Rabbi Slept Late.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi such as Kemelman's sleuth would know Jewish houses of worship well.

clue.text: In principle, lads will catch extremely lachrymose ass

explanation.walkthrough: Mr Bumble's line in Oliver Twist, 'the law is a ass', lets ass stand for LAW. Boyle's Law relates gas pressure and volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The physics rule linking gas pressure and volume is a scientific law, that is, a principle.

clue.text: Declining someone like Doris takes resolute resolution ultimately

indicators.note: only the final letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A determined woman named Doris shows resolve in a resolution.
explanation.walkthrough: Doris Lessing won the 2007 Nobel Prize for Literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Something declining is diminishing or growing smaller.

clue.text: English writer's article written about Haggard novel

She is H. Rider Haggard's novel of the immortal Ayesha

explanation.surface: A literary article on a Rider Haggard novel by an English critic.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Nashe was an Elizabethan pamphleteer and playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Nashe was an Elizabethan satirist and dramatist from England.

clue.text: Put down question to be given to a head of Somerset hotel

explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is an English county in the south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down a rebellion is to suppress or crush it.

clue.text: Chap with a teddy bear seen with Ibsen sat with a novel

clue.text: A weakness of Luzhin possibly wasn't Oedipal happily

explanation.definitionFit: In chess, a pawn without supporting neighbours on adjacent files is a structural weakness, the sort Nabokov's chess master might exploit.

clue.text: Gabonese academic finally gets with a French essayist

explanation.definitionFit: Georges Perec was a French novelist and essayist of the Oulipo group.

clue.text: Enduring royal lies exasperate all reporters at first
